blocks.text: I can sit comfortably and hold a pencil ready for handwriting.

items.title: Get comfortable
items.sub: How to sit and place your paper

items.title: Handwriting patterns
items.sub: Up and down lines and loops

items.def: The way we sit when writing, with our feet on the ground, back straight, and our body balanced and comfortable in a chair.

items.title: Feet
items.sub: Place your feet flat on the floor.

items.title: Back
items.sub: Rest your back against the back of the chair.

items.title: Stomach
items.sub: Gently touch the edge of the table.

blocks.text: If your feet do not reach the floor, you could put them on an upside-down tray or a box. Or you could ask for a smaller chair.

blocks.q: Which are comfortable for handwriting? Tap a position, then tap its column.

items.text: Back against the back of the chair
Stomach touching the edge of the table

blocks.text: The position of the paper is important. We want to see where our pencil is going.

items: Put the paper in line with your writing arm.
If you write with your **right** hand, turn the paper a little to the left.
If you write with your **left** hand, turn the paper a little to the right.
Hold the paper still with your other hand, so it does not slip and slide.

blocks.q: You write with your left hand. How do you turn your paper?
blocks.why: If you write with your left hand, turn the paper a bit to the right so it is in line with your writing arm.

blocks.q: Which hand holds the paper still?
options: The hand that is not writing
blocks.why: We use the other hand, the one that is not writing, to keep the paper still.

blocks.text: Strong hands help us with pencil grip and letter formation.

items: Strong hands help us to write for longer.
In PE you warm up before your main activity. Writing is the same: warm up your hands first.

items.title: Finger touch
items.sub: Touch each finger to your thumb, one at a time.

items.title: Finger tap
items.sub: Tap each finger against your head in turn.

items.title: Finger pull
items.sub: Gently pull each finger in turn.

blocks.text: You can go forwards and backwards with the finger touch. Try it with both hands at once!

items.def: How we hold the pencil with our fingers, so it feels comfortable and steady in our hand.
A special way of holding the pencil with three fingers (thumb, index and middle fingers) that helps us write smoothly and with control.

items: Pointing finger and tall finger go on the top.
Rest your hand on the table.

blocks.text: Rhyme: Pointing finger, tall finger, on the top, thumb goes underneath, yeah!

blocks.q: Which three fingers make the tripod grip?
options: Thumb, pointing finger and tall finger
Thumb, little finger and next finger
blocks.why: The tripod grip uses three fingers: the thumb, the index (pointing) finger and the middle (tall) finger.

blocks.q: Where does your thumb go in the tripod grip?
options: On the top of the pencil
blocks.why: Pointing finger and tall finger go on the top, and the thumb goes underneath.

blocks.text: Handwriting patterns help us to prepare for writing letters.

blocks.q: Match each pattern to the letters it helps with.

items: Keep your pencil on the paper the whole time.
Make strong, straight lines for your up and down lines.
Make continuous loops all the way across the page.

blocks.text: For a loop, go **up, loop, and down**. You can make big ones and tiny ones.

blocks.q: What should your pencil do while you make a pattern?
options: Jump off the paper each time
blocks.why: Keep your pencil on the paper the whole time you make your lines and loops.

items.def: The way we make each letter, starting at the top and following the correct path to create the shape of the letter.

blocks.text: It takes practice to form a letter correctly, just like it takes practice to hold a pencil well.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Some letters need you to lift your pencil to add a dot or a cross.

items.def: Straight, parallel lines that we can use as a guide to help us write neatly and keep our letters the same size.

blocks.text: Tramlines help you to write neatly and keep your letters the same size.

blocks.q: What do tramlines help us to do?
options: Write neatly and keep our letters the same size
blocks.why: Tramlines are a guide to help us write neatly and keep our letters the same size.

blocks.q: Which pattern helps us prepare to write rounded letters?
blocks.why: Practising loops helps us form rounded letters. Up and down lines help with letters that have straight lines.

items: Sit with your feet flat on the floor, your back against the chair and your stomach touching the edge of the table.
Turn your paper in line with your writing arm, and hold it still with your other hand.
Warm up your hands, then hold your pencil in the tripod grip.
Handwriting patterns (up and down lines and loops) get us ready to write letters.
